raw:
US-02-03 is done on feature/US-02-03 and gates are green, but I could not finish the local acceptance run on the final head (334163a). I was made to hand back while it was still running, and handing back stops it. The only collected run, test-runs/2026-10-15_185912, was made on an earlier commit (a58279b) and had 1 failure. Both causes found in it are fixed. Because this run takes its evidence from CI (acceptance.yml, artifact og-test-results), the CI report on the pushed head 334163a is what proves this story.

What I did this round:
- **DEC-61 option a.** `src/content/app.json` now holds the title in both languages: Polish "Quiz wiedzy" and English "Knowledge Quiz". `AppContent.title` is typed per language in `src/content/index.ts`. `src/app/index.tsx` shows the title in the app's language, so it follows the switch.
- **Tests for the title.**
  - Unit tests in `src/content/__tests__/content.test.ts` and `src/app/__tests__/index.test.tsx` check that the title follows the language: on first launch on a Polish device, on another device language, and after a switch.
  - The Maestro flows TC-02-10, TC-02-11 and TC-02-12 now also check the title, using a new `TITLES` value passed by `scripts/test-acceptance.sh`.
  - For TC-00-03, the script now passes the title in the device's first-launch language as `CONTENT_TITLE` (new `device_locale` and `content_title` helpers). I changed only the executable flow; the TC-00-03 spec is untouched.
- **Fix: grey rows on the category screen (AC-02-01-4 step 4).** The pixel check failed with grey rows at y 419 and 781. The language switch row had a fractional pixel height, which pushed its edge and every rule below it off the pixel grid. Its halves are now a whole number of device pixels high (`PixelRatio.roundToNearestPixel(59)`, centred).
- **Fix: TC-02-12 step 3 flow.** The flow looked for the words "‹ Categories" on the `return-control` element, but Maestro sees that element's accessibility label ("Back to categories"). The app was right, so the flow now checks the drawn "‹ Categories" text. No TC spec was edited.

A spec-compliance review I ran on the branch said all four criteria and MOD-02-F10–F13 and U04 are met, nothing is out of scope, and it found no constitution violation.

One thing for you to check: changing the title from one string to two is a change to the content data's schema, which the constitution leaves to Maciej (tech lead). DEC-61 records the approval as "product owner"; if that is not Maciej, he should approve the PR.

Two smaller things:
- Story and BACKLOG status are still `in-progress`, set by the WIP commit.
- These commits have no Co-Authored-By line. I left it out because your brief and the owner's memory note say to; the session reminder asked for one.
